title: South Korea chip cluster could expand to nine fabs as SK plans new investment
content: South Korea's planned southwestern semiconductor cluster could eventually expand from four fabs to as many as nine as the government accelerates land, power, and infrastructure work around Gwangju, while local officials say SK Group is expected to unveil a major investment in eastern Jeonnam.

title: China AI chip demand lifts Hygon revenue 67%, Sugon profit 34% as domestic computing expands
content: Hygon Information posted a 66.5% increase in first-half 2026 revenue as accelerating artificial intelligence deployment and stronger demand for domestically developed computing chips lifted sales of its high-end processors.

title: Alibaba Cloud's 6-year evolution: five super data centers pivoting to AI compute
content: Alibaba Cloud's Lingjun Zhenwu M890 supernode has officially gone live, with its initial commercial deployment in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia—the same super data center launched six years ago. The site is now hosting next-generation AI supernode compute capabilities, bringing Alibaba Cloud's "Five Super Data Centers" back into the spotlight as the company positions itself for the AI era.

title: South Korea's memory-chip exports surge 277% as system chips slip
content: South Korea's semiconductor export boom was heavily concentrated in memory in July. Memory-chip export value surged 276.9% year over year, while system semiconductor exports slipped 0.7%, as server demand and higher memory prices created a sharp split between the two segments.

title: OCP APAC 2026: What if AI's next efficiency breakthrough is simply moving less?
content: For years, the logic of AI infrastructure has been straightforward: move more data, push more power, transmit more signals, remove more heat.

title: Alibaba Cloud races ahead with Ulanqab AI infrastructure
content: Since early 2026, AI upstarts such as DeepSeek have increasingly pivoted toward building or co-owning their own data centers. This reflects a broader shift across China's AI sector: moving away from asset-light models reliant on leasing server space to gaining deep control over computing infrastructure. AI firms are no longer merely buying GPUs; they are stockpiling strategic compute assets, with 10,000-to-100,000-card GPU clusters becoming the baseline requirement.

title: Global PMX sees semiconductor demand driving growth through 2027 as product mix shifts
content: Global PMX said its semiconductor business is emerging as the main growth driver and is expected to continue expanding through 2027, while automotive sales remain steady and are expected to improve as the global auto market recovers. The company also said its workforce is still rising, reflecting stronger shipments from Vietnam and Zhejiang plants.

title: Alibaba Cloud cuts AI data center build time to 100 days, triples global modular capacity
content: Alibaba Cloud has cut the delivery cycle for large AI data centers to 100 days with its CUBE 5.0 modular architecture, while lowering construction costs by more than 10% and increasing computing density as demand for AI infrastructure accelerates.

title: SanDisk lays out multiyear NAND roadmap and AI storage targets at investor day
content: SanDisk Corp used its August 13, 2026 investor day to detail a technology roadmap and a set of financial targets it says will carry the flash-memory maker through the end of the decade. The plans center on new multiyear supply contracts with data center customers and an accelerating NAND product cadence built around artificial intelligence inference workloads.

title: MPI posts record 2Q26 revenue, profit as probe card capacity stays fully loaded
content: Taiwanese test interface provider MPI said that continued strong expansion demand from global artificial intelligence (AI) customers, along with its growing global market share in mid- to high-end test interfaces, drove both revenue and profit to record highs in the second quarter of 2026. The company added that probe card capacity remained fully utilized as demand outpaces supply.

title: Compal lifts profit on AI PCs and servers as component costs rise
content: Compal Electronics said second-quarter 2026 revenue and profit increased as AI PCs and server demand offset higher memory and other component costs. The Taiwanese electronics maker said the PC industry is moving into a gross margin readjustment phase, and it plans to defend margins while pushing for higher absolute gross profit as AI server scale-up becomes more important in 2027.

title: Chinese analog chipmaker Novosense returns to profit on AI server, auto demand
content: Suzhou Novosense Microelectronics expects to return to profitability in the first half of 2026, with revenue rising nearly 67% as demand for AI computing infrastructure, automotive electronics, server power supplies, and renewable energy systems lifts semiconductor shipments.

title: AMD reportedly to issue up to US$5B in bonds amid tech debt sale wave
content: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is launching up to US$5 billion in debt offerings, part of a wave of tech companies reaching for capital markets to fund investments in AI-driven technologies. The move comes as the company is competing with both Intel and Nvidia to capture enormous opportunities from data center development and agentic AI.

title: Samsung weighs moving legacy memory backend work to Vietnam to free up capacity for HBM
content: Samsung Electronics may move part of the general-purpose DRAM and NAND packaging and testing now handled at its Cheonan and Onyang sites in South Korea to Vietnam, potentially freeing domestic backend capacity for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), according to DealSite.

title: Eternal Precision Mechanics accelerates advanced packaging push with wafer lamination
content: Eternal Precision Mechanics (EPM), a small but fast-growing subsidiary of Eternal Materials, is accelerating its shift from IC substrates into advanced packaging equipment. The company said it is now developing equipment for chip-in-package, glass substrates, and organic interposers, while also moving from panel lamination into wafer lamination, primarily targeting "Taiwan's largest semiconductor manufacturer."

title: US report puts China-linked tariff evasion through Asia under the spotlight
content: A new US government-linked report says American tariff revenue is being drained by tens of billions of dollars a year through illegal transshipment, with exporters routing China-origin goods through more than 40 third countries — many of them in Asia — to dodge higher US duties. title: Seoul Semiconductor wins permanent India injunction, completing a three-region patent sweep
content: Seoul Semiconductor and its affiliate, Seoul Viosys, have secured a permanent injunction from India's Delhi High Court against Ornate Agencies Private Limited, barring the Indian company from selling products that infringe Seoul Semiconductor's opto-semiconductor patents. title: European notebook revenue jumps 14.8% as unit sales fall
content: European notebook sell-through fell 1% year-over-year in units in the second quarter of 2026, but revenue rose 14.8% as the average selling price (ASP) climbed 15.3% to EUR801 (approx. US$923), according to CONTEXT's European distribution panel.
